prompt:
A 3-column by 2-row grid of 6 circular pirate achievement badge emblems, hand-painted game-art style, soft painterly shading and a beveled metal rim. Each badge is a round medallion coin centered in its own cell with generous transparent margin around it. Transparent background. No text, no numbers, no letters anywhere. No glow, no halos, no light rays, no glowing edges, no emissive or luminous effects on anything. Consistent lighting, consistent medallion size across all six. Each badge's metal tier: bronze = humble, silver = accomplished, gold = elite, ornate jeweled gold = legendary. No faces and no figures anywhere in this set: the thing that was fought is shown only through what it left behind.

Read left-to-right, top row then bottom row:

One Last Ride (gold) — a colossal broken jawbone arch of pale ancient bone rising out of black water, one small intact ship sailing out through the gap beneath it.
Cut Off at the Wrist (gold) — an enormous drowned hand sinking wrist-first into black water with a cutlass driven clean through the wrist, pale bubbles trailing upward.
The Long Quiet (bronze) — dead flat black water closing over a vast dark shape barely visible below the surface, one last silver bubble rising, a still sea under a pale night sky.
Colours of the Hand (gold) — three ship hulls fanned out side by side like a dealt hand of cards, one bone white, one deep indigo, one dark crimson, sails furled.
Salvor's Claim (bronze) — a single freshly framed crew berth built into the salvaged rib cage of a great wreck, raw new timber lashed against ancient pale bone, a hammock and a lantern hung inside it.
Both Hands (gold) — two crew berths framed side by side inside the same salvaged wreck ribs, each fitted out with its own hammock and lantern.
